questions.question_text:
A hospital investigates the waiting times of all patients it saw in April. It records the waiting time of every one of those $3280$ patients.
Which statement identifies the population and correctly classifies the collection?

options.text: The population is all $3280$ patients seen in April; the collection is a census.
The population is all $3280$ patients seen in April; the collection is a sample.
options.why: Calls the collection a sample even though every member of the population is included.

options.text: The population is all patients the hospital has ever seen; the collection is a sample.
options.why: Widens the population beyond the patients seen in April, which is the group being investigated.

options.text: The population is the patients seen in April who waited longest; the collection is a census.
options.why: Restricts the population to one subgroup even though the investigation concerns all patients seen in April.

questions.solution_text:
Population: **all $3280$ patients seen by the hospital in April**.
This is a **census** because every patient in that population is included.

questions.question_text:
A council tests $25$ of the $900$ streetlights in a suburb to estimate how many of the suburb's streetlights need replacing.
What is the population?

options.text: All $900$ streetlights in the suburb.
The $25$ streetlights that were tested.
options.why: Names the sample rather than the population.

options.text: The streetlights in the suburb that need replacing.
options.why: Restricts the population to the streetlights needing replacement, although the investigation concerns all streetlights in the suburb.

options.text: All streetlights in the state.
options.why: Widens the population beyond the group the council is investigating.

questions.solution_text:
The council wants to know about the streetlights in the suburb.
That group is every individual being studied.
Population: all $900$ streetlights in the suburb.

questions.question_text:
A producer investigates the masses of all $2400$ eggs packed that morning. It weighs $80$ eggs from that production.
Which statement identifies the population and correctly classifies the collection?

options.text: The population is all $2400$ eggs packed that morning; the collection is a sample.
The population is the $80$ eggs weighed; the collection is a census.
options.why: Treats the eggs selected for measurement as the whole population instead of all eggs being investigated.

options.text: The population is all $2400$ eggs packed that morning; the collection is a census.
options.why: Calls the collection a census even though only $80$ eggs are weighed.

options.text: The population is all eggs the producer has ever packed; the collection is a sample.
options.why: Widens the population beyond that morning's production.

questions.solution_text:
Population: **all $2400$ eggs packed that morning**.
This is a **sample** because only $80$ eggs are weighed.

questions.question_text:
A council investigates the water use of all $5400$ households in a town during a particular week. It collects that week's water-use records from $240$ households.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The population is all $5400$ households in the town; the collection is a sample.
The population is the $240$ households whose records were collected; the collection is a census.
options.why: Confuses the households selected for data collection with the whole group being investigated.

options.text: The population is all $5400$ households in the town; the collection is a census.
options.why: Calls a collection from only part of the population a census.

options.text: The population is all households in the state; the collection is a sample.
options.why: Widens the population beyond the town named in the investigation.

questions.solution_text:
Population: **all $5400$ households in the town**.
This is a **sample** because records are collected from only $240$ households.

questions.question_text:
A school investigates the results of all $210$ students who sat an exam. It examines every student's result.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The population is all $210$ students who sat the exam; the collection is a census.
The population is all $210$ students who sat the exam; the collection is a sample.
options.why: Calls the collection a sample even though every student's result is examined.

options.text: The population is all students at the school; the collection is a sample.
options.why: Includes students who did not sit the exam, although the investigation concerns only those who did.

options.text: The population is only students who passed the exam; the collection is a census.
options.why: Restricts the population to students who passed, although the investigation includes every student who sat the exam.

questions.solution_text:
Population: **all $210$ students who sat the exam**.
This is a **census** because every student's result is examined.

questions.question_text:
A rope maker investigates the breaking strain of a batch of $4500$ ropes. It tests $16$ ropes from that batch to destruction.
What is the population?

options.text: All $4500$ ropes in the batch.
The $16$ ropes tested.
options.why: Names the sample tested rather than the whole batch being investigated.

options.text: Every rope the maker has ever produced.
options.why: Widens the population beyond the particular batch being investigated.

options.text: Only the ropes in the batch with the greatest breaking strain.
options.why: Restricts the population to one subgroup even though the investigation concerns the whole batch.

questions.solution_text:
The investigation concerns the batch.
Population: **all $4500$ ropes in the batch**.

questions.question_text:
A national sports body investigates the training times of all registered junior swimmers in the country. It surveys every one of the $92$ registered junior swimmers at one club and separately surveys $720$ registered junior swimmers selected nationally. Each collection includes only part of the country's registered junior swimmers.
How should the two collections be classified?

options.text: Both collections are samples of the country's registered junior swimmers.
The club collection is a census and the national collection is a sample.
options.why: Treats surveying every junior swimmer at one club as surveying the whole national population.

options.text: Both collections are censuses of the country's registered junior swimmers.
options.why: Calls both collections censuses even though neither includes the whole national population.

options.text: The club collection is a sample and the national collection is a census.
options.why: Treats selecting swimmers nationally as including every registered junior swimmer in the country.

questions.solution_text:
Population: **all registered junior swimmers in the country**.
Both collections are **samples** because each includes only part of that population.

questions.question_text:
Scientists investigate the salt content of the water in a lake. They collect $2000$ mL of water from the lake to analyse.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The population is all water in the lake; the collection is a sample.
The population is the $2000$ mL collected; the collection is a census.
options.why: Treats the collected water as the whole population rather than part of the lake's water.

options.text: The population is all water in the lake; the collection is a census.
options.why: Calls the collection a census even though only part of the lake's water is collected.

options.text: The population is all water in every lake; the collection is a sample.
options.why: Widens the population beyond the particular lake being investigated.

questions.solution_text:
Population: **all water in the lake**.
This is a **sample** because only $2000$ mL of the lake's water is collected.
